config.EnableMarriageContent.description: Enable the two stories at fourteen hearts.
config.EnableArthurHomeOffice.descriptio: Animate Arthur’s work at his desk.
config.EnableSVECompatibility.descriptio: Use the alternate entrance with SVE.
config.EnableOptionalCompatibilityPatche: Enable the optional SVE and LittleNPCs patches.
Allow vanilla villagers to mention Arthur.
npc.name: Arthur
gift.love: This is going in my emergency deadline kit. Thanks!$1
gift.like: Good pick. I was about to take a break.$1
gift.dislike: I’m probably the wrong person for this. Thanks for thinking of me.
gift.hate: Did that come out of the trash? I’ll leave it here.
gift.neutral: Thanks, @. I’ll see what I can do with it.
event.h02.1: The mug with the crooked handle is mine. It was the first thing I unpacked that felt like home.
event.h02.2: Come look. I make signs and book covers. This draft is for a bakery in Zuzu that wants people to recognize it from across the street.
event.h02.3: Yesterday I ate lunch on the step and watched a beetle fall off a leaf three times. I can't remember the last time I took that long to eat.$2
event.h02.4: If the light's on, you can knock. Sometimes I forget to take a break until somebody comes by.
event.h04.1: I put the game on easy. That's our secret. Ours and the goose that just took your last life.$2
event.h04.2: Wait, you can pick up the fence? I've been trying to jump it for three weeks.$4
event.h04.3: Hand me the other controller. I'll distract the goose. If this works, I want a flattering portrait on the victory screen.
event.h04.4: We won! I don't even remember what I was rushing to finish before you got here. One more round?$1
event.h06.1: I've been staring at the same page since breakfast. Every time I make a mark I can hear the client asking what it's supposed to be.$8
event.h06.2: He once said an early draft looked unfinished. It was unfinished. I still hear that every time I start over.
event.h06.choice: What should we do?#Start with one ugly line.#Take a break outside.
event.h06.reply1: A prize for worst line. That sounds attainable.$2
event.h06.reply2: A lap of the yard first. I’ll leave the file open for when we get back.$1
event.h06.3: I think I'm trying to reach the part where somebody likes it before I've done the part where I draw it.$9
event.h06.4: I'll keep that crooked line. Tomorrow I want to remember that I finally let one stay.$1
event.h08.1: I came up here the day my last box arrived. I'd forgotten what it was like to hear a branch snap and know where the sound came from.
event.h08.2: In my game, the path through the hills changes depending on what you stop to look at. I wanted walking slowly to do something.
event.h08.3: There's a bakery in Zuzu I'll miss for the rest of my life. When I think about where to go at the end of the day, it's still this house.$9
event.h08.4: I wanted you to see this spot. You're one of the first people I think of when I find a place worth coming back to.$1
event.h10.1: When you gave me the bouquet, I stood in front of the sink for five minutes. I'd forgotten where I kept the vase.$6
event.h10.2: I want to be with you on days when supper's leftovers and there's a sock behind the door. I keep thinking about days like that.$11
event.h10.choice: What do you say?#Yes.#I’d like to wait.
event.h10.wait: Of course. Could we stay here a little longer anyway?$1
event.h10.4: I think I'm going to remember your face just then for a very long time.$11
event.h14a.1: Look what I found in the drawer. The first thing I drew after I moved here was the key. I kept mixing it up with the mailbox key.
event.h14a.2: My game's ready for someone else to play. I want to see what you notice before I tell you what I meant to do.
event.h14a.3: You went straight to the window. I put it in after the wedding, when I kept looking up at the light on our kitchen wall.$9
event.h14a.4: Meet me at the lookout later. I've got one last thing to draw.
event.h14b.1: I deleted the thank-you screen. It sounded like somebody accepting a prize for a game nobody had played yet.
event.h14b.2: I'll put a path behind the last house. There'll be room for two people to walk side by side.
event.h14b.3: Last Tuesday we spent forty minutes figuring out who'd bought the jam. I don't remember what I finished at work that day.$2
event.h14b.4: I want to keep making things. And I want to be home in time to hear what happened while I was out.$11
event.family.1: I moved my sketchbooks here to make room at the farm. Tiny socks take up a surprising amount of space.
event.family.2: I warmed my tea three times yesterday. Every time I sat down, I heard the little sound that means I'm needed.
event.family.3: I don't always know what the sound means. I'm learning to try one thing and then another.$8
event.family.4: Can we take turns getting a whole cup of something warm today? I can go second.$1
event.family_prep.1: I made a list of things we'd need if we ever welcomed a child. I got as far as little shirts before I realized I wanted to talk to you.$6
event.family_prep.2: Whenever I picture being a dad, I picture doing something I already know. Drawing an animal or fixing a shelf. I'd like to learn the rest with you.
event.family_prep.3: We can keep that drawer empty as long as we want. It felt important to tell you what I was thinking.
event.family_two.1: I put two hooks by the door, one low and one very low. There's already an argument about which belongs to whom.
event.family_two.2: When I was little, I told stories into the drawer under my bed. It was the only place I thought nobody could interrupt me.
event.family_two.3: I'd like each of our kids to have a spot like that. Maybe we could start by asking where they go when they want quiet.$9
event.deadline.1: The bakery opens tomorrow. I promised the signs before lunch, then spent half an hour drawing a pigeon that won't appear on any of them.
event.deadline.2: I sent the draft with bigger letters. The baker said she could read it from across the street. I'd been fretting over the edge of the loaf.
event.deadline.3: I'm going outside before I find a reason to turn the computer back on.$1
event.rules.1: Sam says a good game lets you pause in a boss fight. Abigail says a good boss can wait while you answer the door.
event.rules.2: I made the boss say hello when you come back. Now the giant eel sounds disappointed in me.$5
event.rules.3: Maybe nobody needs to explain why they stopped playing. I should try putting that in the manual.
event.rainwalk.1: There's a leak in my umbrella. If I turn it just right, it waters the plants when I stop on the step.
event.rainwalk.2: I'd like the rain to last a little longer today. My coffee's in a flask and the path is empty.
event.rainwalk.3: Watch that dip. I've already donated one dry sock to it.$2
event.sketch.1: Leah asked me to draw the same tree in ten minutes, one minute and ten seconds. The ten-second tree is the only one that looks alive.
event.sketch.2: Here, try one. I'll turn the page so you can start wherever you like.
event.sketch.3: Years from now I want to see what each of us thought this spot looked like.$1
event.birthday.1: Robin dropped off a toolbox. Apparently she trusts me with my own hinges now.$2
event.birthday.2: I've got two forks and a cake that keeps leaning to the left. Can you help me with the left side?
event.birthday.3: Everyone in Zuzu keeps asking what I'm doing for my birthday. At the moment I'm cutting you a piece.
event.dinner.1: Sam brought bread. Sebastian brought hot sauce. I asked for a vegetable and got a note that said tomatoes are fruit.
event.dinner.Sam: I would have brought a vegetable if it was going on a pizza.
event.dinner.Sebastian: The note has citations. I left them at home because you took my stapler.
event.dinner.2: You can start on the soup. I want to see your face before somebody drowns it in hot sauce.
event.dinner.3: One of these bowls used to hold spare screws. I'm very glad everyone came anyway.$2
event.tideline.1: I brought my shoes home full of sand again. Somewhere the beach is getting slightly smaller because of me.
event.tideline.2: I tried drawing the same stretch at two tides. The second picture's mostly a smudge. A wave got to the page first.
event.tideline.3: That's the page I'm keeping. It reminds me of what wet shoes sound like.$2
event.film.1: There's a train in this film that never stops. Penny said it's a metaphor. Ten minutes in, I think it's a terrible train service.
event.film.2: I like the woman with the red bag. She moves it so a stranger can sit. You can tell she's done it a thousand times.
event.film.3: Mind if we leave the lights off a little longer? I like it when the room takes a minute to come back.
event.prototype.1: That's my game on the monitor. You can open a door and walk straight through the hill if you take a left on the other side.
event.prototype.2: Sebastian says I should fix the hill. I want us to walk through it once before it stops being possible.
event.prototype.3: There it is. The whole underside of the map. I haven't drawn anything there, so for now it's ours.$10
event.playtest.1: I asked Abigail to tell me what she did while she played. She spent four minutes trying to open a window.
event.playtest.Abigail: I wanted to see if the neighbor had a light on. I could hear their radio.
event.playtest.2: I'd drawn the window to catch the light. She thought she could lean out. Now I know what I'm doing on Saturday.
event.playtest.3: When she got to the end, she asked where the lonely character goes next. I'd been so busy with the controls I forgot someone might care.$1
event.invoice.1: My first invoice from this house cleared. I made tea and forgot to send the message to the person I wanted to tell.
event.invoice.2: The bakery hired me again. This time we agreed on two drafts and I asked for a deposit before opening the file.
event.invoice.3: I'm putting some aside to pay Sebastian for his time. He'll insist it's a favor. The invoice will win.
event.evening.1: I said I'd be out here at five. I'd blame the client, but the client sent the last email yesterday.$7
event.evening.2: I kept opening the same file because I wanted to be proud of where I'd left it. I ended up undoing every change.
event.evening.3: Tomorrow I'll close it at five even if I'm halfway through something. We've still got half a walk tonight, if you want it.
dialogue.Introduction: Hi! I'm Arthur. If you saw someone carrying a monitor up the mountain last week, that was me. If you saw him drop it, that was somebody else.$2
dialogue.AcceptBouquet: I'd been trying to think of a casual way to ask you out. I can design twelve logos in a week and still freeze over one sentence. Yes, @.$6
dialogue.RejectBouquet_LowHearts: I like getting to know you. Could we give ourselves a little more time?
dialogue.RejectBouquet_VeryLowHearts: That's a big question for people who barely know each other. Could we start with lunch?
dialogue.RejectMermaidPendant_Under10Hea: I want us to talk about what our days together would be like before we pick a date.
dialogue.RejectMermaidPendant_NeedHouseU: I'd love to talk about moving in. Shall we make some room for both of us first?
dialogue.breakUp: I'm sad, but I hear you. I'll take a little time to get used to this.$7
dialogue.divorced: Hi, @. I'm keeping my days simple for a while. Can we leave it at hello today?
dialogue.WipedMemory: Hey! Have we met? I'm trying to figure out which mug at the Saloon holds the most. Want to help?
dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Loved: You remembered both the date and what I like? That's dangerously good detective work, @.$2
dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Positive: I'd planned to spend my birthday doing invoices. This is a much better afternoon.$1
dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Negative: I'm glad you stopped by. This particular gift might be happier going home with you.$5
dialogue.GreenRain: I unplugged the drawing tablet. If the sky wants to experiment with color, it can use its own equipment.$4
dialogue.GreenRain_2: I bought a green notebook last year to sketch this weather. I opened it today and realized I couldn't see my pencil marks.$5
dialogue.FlowerDance_Accept: Yes! I practiced with a chair. You'll be pleased to know the chair made it out in one piece.$2
dialogue.FlowerDance_Accept_Spouse: If either of us forgets the turn, use the signal we practiced in the kitchen.$1
dialogue.FlowerDance_Decline: I think I'll watch this round. Ask me another year?
dialogue.SpouseGiftJealous: When I saw the {1} you gave {0}, I felt a little off. Can we talk later? I'd rather tell you how I felt than guess.$8
dialogue.SpouseStardrop: I wanted to give you something from me that didn't come with a deadline. Hold out your hands.$11
dialogue.SpouseFarmhouseClutter: I couldn't get to the counter without stepping on something. I left the breakfast supplies where I could reach them.
dialogue.Spouse_MonstersInHouse: Are you hurt? We'll figure out how it got in once we know nothing else is moving.
dialogue.RejectGift_Divorced: I'm all right, thanks. I'd rather leave gifts out of things for now.
dialogue.MovieInvitation: I'll bring a notebook that fits in my coat. If the movie's good, it'll stay there.
dialogue.Resort: I watched the tide erase my footprints. Imagine if my project folders cleaned themselves up like that.$9
dialogue.Resort_EnteringResort: I packed everything except a pencil. Maybe that was my brain's idea of a holiday.
dialogue.Resort_Leaving: I'm emptying my shoes before I leave. There are limits to my interest in texture.
dialogue.Resort_Bar: A paper umbrella feels a lot like finally getting the out-of-office reply right.$1
dialogue.Resort_Shore: That line where the wet sand stops is impossible to draw from memory. I've tried.
dialogue.Resort_Wander: I came looking for smooth stones and spent twenty minutes watching a crab dig.
dialogue.Resort_Chair: I meant to sketch a palm tree. Fifteen minutes later I was drawing the pattern the chair left on my leg.
dialogue.Resort_Dance: No one here knows the version of me that practices first. I'm curious how long I can get away with it.$2
dialogue.Resort_Towel: I moved the towel twice and still found a patch of hot sand. I think it's following me.
dialogue.Resort_Umbrella: From here I can see four sets of feet. I think I know which one's getting up for something cold next.
dialogue.Mon: The hardest part of freelancing is making your own Monday. The second hardest part is convincing yourself it ends at six.
dialogue.Tue: I take a list to Pierre's now. Otherwise I come out with flour, jam and no idea what I was going to make.
dialogue.Wed: I drew a tree this morning and realized halfway through that I was drawing the spaces between the branches.$9
dialogue.Thu: Penny found me a book with birds in the margins. The index doesn't mention birds. Someone just decided the pages needed company.
dialogue.Fri: Sam said my job on his team was to provide a calming presence. I think I'm being benched politely.$2
dialogue.Sat: Sebastian and I are testing if a person fixes a bug faster when someone else makes the tea. Important research.
dialogue.Sun: I turned off my notifications. If civilization collapses before dinner, tell it I'll answer Monday.
dialogue.Mon2: I still pay for a desk in Zuzu. It took me three months to admit I'm paying to keep the option of going back.
dialogue.Tue2: I bought a strawberry because it had a green stripe shaped like lightning. I almost forgot to eat it after I drew it.
dialogue.Wed2: Leah taught me to follow the branch with my eyes before making a mark. I look at trees for longer now.
dialogue.Thu2: I used to draw new covers for library books when the real ones went missing. I guess I chose my job at nine.
dialogue.Fri2: Shane told me the jukebox skips a beat in the third song. Now neither of us can hear anything else.
dialogue.Sat2: Abigail chooses the weakest character on purpose. I've still never beaten her.
dialogue.Sun2: I used to call home from the subway so we'd have an excuse when the signal dropped. Here I have to actually say goodbye.
dialogue.Mon4: I leave the last revision open while I make dinner. Then I ask whether I'd change it if someone else had drawn it.
dialogue.Tue4: Robin made me bring a box the size of the desk before tightening the doorframe. I was offended by how right she was.
dialogue.Wed4: A fox crossed the trail while I was sharpening my pencil. I got the tail and made up the rest.
dialogue.Thu4: My test for a picture book is whether Penny can close it halfway through and still have the kids argue about what's on the next page.
dialogue.Fri4: The first time I came here I picked the smallest table. Now Gus brings another chair before I've ordered.
dialogue.Sat4: Sam sampled my kettle for a song. Now I expect a drum fill when the water boils.
dialogue.Sun4: I think I've made a real friend here. I can say I'm tired and still get invited next week.
dialogue.Mon6: I told a client I couldn't start until Friday. They said Friday was fine. Forty minutes of rehearsal for eleven seconds on the phone.
dialogue.Tue6: That bench that's always a little damp is in my game. You can sit on it, but your character gives you a look.
dialogue.Wed6: Leah asked to see my Rejected folder and picked three sketches I'd forgotten I liked.
dialogue.Thu6: Penny asked if my game's character ever gets to ask for help. I said of course. Then I had to go home and write a new scene.
dialogue.Fri6: I said yes to every deadline in case they never asked again. They always ask again. Usually at eleven at night.
dialogue.Sat6: Sebastian and I spent the afternoon fixing one door. He patched the code. I got to decide whether it creaked.
dialogue.Sun6: I kept the packing boxes in case moving here was a mistake. Yesterday I cut one up for a sketch board.
dialogue.Mon8: Can I show you an unfinished sketch? You always ask what I was trying to draw. That's a good question to hear early.
dialogue.Tue8: I wrote your advice on a receipt. The other side says two bags of flour. It's the most important paper on my desk.
dialogue.Wed8: There's an empty page at the end of this book. Next time we walk uphill, want to decide together what goes there?
dialogue.Thu8: You can take something from my shelf now and I won't pretend I have a system.
dialogue.Fri8: I told Gus to save you a seat. He said he'd been putting one out for months.
dialogue.Sat8: I put a second controller in the drawer that opens properly. You're officially a regular.$1
dialogue.Sun8: I like spending a day with someone without either of us having to fill every quiet minute.
dialogue.spring_17_*: My birthday wish is to spend as little of the day as possible resetting passwords.$1
dialogue.spring_2_1: I carried a box marked cables up the hill. It contained six sweaters. Past Arthur is an unreliable narrator.
dialogue.spring_9_*: The first flowers grow low. I crouched to draw them and needed the fence to get back up.
dialogue.spring_21_*: I'm trying to match the color of wet cherry bark. I've made a convincing bruise so far.
dialogue.summer_3_*: My drawing tablet gets warm in the afternoon. I set a cold mug next to it and forgot what I was drawing.
dialogue.summer_14_*: I took off my shoes before checking the sand. My sprint to the water is now a personal best.
dialogue.summer_20_*: Someone turned catching a specific fish into a whole weekend. I've been underrating what people will show up for.
dialogue.summer_21_*: You can tell who's got a bite at the derby even if you only draw their shoulders.
dialogue.summer_23_*: The fireflies look like someone's saving a game one little light at a time.
dialogue.fall_2_*: I said I'd wait for the leaves to change before picking colors. Then I saw the pears.
dialogue.fall_13_*: They asked for a little more harvest in the illustration. One version has a basket. In the other, the pumpkin gets the entire page.
dialogue.fall_25_*: I put the leaf back after I drew it. I can still check the color tomorrow if the wind leaves it alone.
dialogue.winter_3_*: I'm drawing snow with no white pencil. Most of the work is figuring out the shadows.
dialogue.winter_10_*: The kettle sounds different when it snows. Or I'm finally quiet enough to notice.
dialogue.winter_12_*: I can't feel my fingers. The squid don't seem to consider that a reason to make things easier.
dialogue.winter_13_*: I showed Willy three squid I drew yesterday. Apparently one of them is a knot in a rope.
dialogue.winter_15_*: I want to sketch the market before the lights come on. The first boat to light up gets the whole page.
dialogue.winter_16_*: I'd like a game menu that sounds like a boat at the market. Imagine hearing the water every time you choose something.
dialogue.winter_17_*: I bought a tiny lamp. It lights up two pencils and exactly one knuckle.$2
dialogue.winter_27_*: I bought a calendar with room to write go out. Last year's barely had room for all the work.
dialogue.AcceptGift_(O)206: The first time I asked if Gus delivered, he handed me the box and opened the door. This is much better.$2
dialogue.AcceptGift_(O)220: I'm finding a plate. Last time I ate cake over the keyboard, I found a crumb at the next deadline.
dialogue.AcceptGift_(O)233: I know a shady spot three minutes away. Looking at the cone, we've got two.$2
dialogue.AcceptGift_(O)253: The good stuff! I'll drink it slowly. That should take about ten seconds.$10
dialogue.AcceptGift_(O)400: The red on this side is different from the red on that side. Give me a second before I eat it.$9
dialogue.AcceptGift_(O)421: This goes by the monitor. If I spend my day looking at a rectangle, I want something next to it that refuses to be one.
weather.rain: The rain makes the valley sound like a room full of people turning pages.$9
weather.storm: One loud crack and suddenly every file is called FINAL FOR REAL.$4
romance.Mon10: I’m keeping the end of Monday free. Want to spend some of it together?$11
romance.Fri10: Want to walk home together after the Saloon? The long way, if you have time.$11
follow.h02: The crooked mug is still by the kettle. I found another crooked mug to keep it company.
follow.h04: If the goose asks, we retired undefeated. The games I played alone don’t count.$2
follow.h06: I kept the first mark we made. It’s underneath the finished drawing.
progress.ccIsComplete: The afternoon light lands on the boards in the Community Center. Next time Penny reads there, I want to paint it.
progress.JojaMember: A Joja contract paid my rent once. I spent a week making the words BUY LOCAL look the same in twenty different towns.
marriage.Indoor_Day_0: I moved your mug away from the edge. Mine's usually the one that falls, so I'm calling this progress.
marriage.Indoor_Day_1: I'll send the files before lunch. After that, can you help me decide where the hooks should go?
marriage.Indoor_Day_2: I made toast. The good slices are under the plate. The others are a lesson in distraction.
marriage.Indoor_Day_3: I moved over to your side of the bed after you got up. I finally understand the appeal of mornings.$11
marriage.Indoor_Day_4: What are you doing today? I'm trying to ask before offering to do something that might get in your way.
marriage.Rainy_Day_0: These windows seal better than the old ones. I still reach for a towel whenever it starts raining.
marriage.Rainy_Day_1: Leave your coat by the stove when you get back. I'll hang mine next to it and we'll see which dries first.
marriage.Rainy_Day_2: The client said to take my time. I wrote it down before I could convince myself they hadn't meant it.
marriage.Rainy_Day_3: I opened the first drawer and found four versions of the same sketch. Cleaning the office can wait.
marriage.Rainy_Day_4: I'm leaving messages unread until the kettle goes off. We've got time to sit down first.
marriage.Indoor_Night_0: I set out two forks before knowing what we're having. I just like knowing you'll be here for dinner.
marriage.Indoor_Night_1: I went out for a desk lamp and came home with bulbs for the whole house. I can finally see the dust behind the shelf.
marriage.Indoor_Night_2: Can I tell you the three-minute version of a work story? You can tell me whether it sounds like a ten-minute problem.
marriage.Indoor_Night_3: I sketched your boots. One heel wears faster than the other. I thought you might want to see that.
marriage.Indoor_Night_4: I like the light under the door when you're the last one up. Give me a minute and I'll turn it off with you.$11
marriage.Rainy_Night_0: I left the striped towel by the door. It actually absorbs water. I'm not sure what the other one thinks its job is.
marriage.Rainy_Night_1: I put a mixing bowl under the leak. If you hear percussion, that's the window.
marriage.Rainy_Night_2: Want soup? I made enough for two people and one of those nights when one person feels like three.
marriage.Rainy_Night_3: I'm wearing that cardigan with the hole in the sleeve. As far as I'm concerned, the hole came first.
marriage.Rainy_Night_4: Leave the window open a crack? I like falling asleep to rain, as long as it can't reach me.
marriage.Rainy_Night_5: The sky looks like wet newsprint. I went to write that down and found your grocery list in my notebook.$9
marriage.funLeave_ArthurANB: I need a change of scene. I'm taking my sketchbook and leaving the work phone here on purpose.
marriage.funReturn_ArthurANB: I went out looking for an idea and came back wanting to finish the one I already had. How was your day?
marriage.spouseRoom_ArthurANB: I left a drawer empty. I know your things have a place, but there's room here if you need it.
marriage.patio_ArthurANB: The paper keeps moving in the breeze. This corner of the farm is getting an energetic portrait.$1
marriage.Outdoor_ArthurANB: I watched you cut through the field. I never would've known to draw that shortcut.
marriage.OneKid_0: I warmed my mug twice this morning. The little one finally fell asleep, so I drank it cold in celebration.
marriage.OneKid_1: %kid1 hid behind the curtain with both feet showing. I took the long way around to give the spot a chance.
marriage.OneKid_2: I put away the good pencils and left crayons out. Five minutes later there was something on the page I'd never think to draw.
marriage.OneKid_3: I had an answer ready, then realized %kid1 wanted to know why the moon follows us. We'll look again tonight.
marriage.OneKid_4: I can take the next round if you want a quiet walk. Bring me one interesting thing you saw?$1
marriage.TwoKids_0: %kid1 wanted both cups after %kid2 chose a favorite. I made tea in a measuring jug to give everyone time to cool down.
marriage.TwoKids_1: I bought identical pencils. Apparently one has better yellow.
marriage.TwoKids_2: I'm writing down words they invent. If they let me, my game might finally have some decent place names.
marriage.TwoKids_3: Could you take %kid2 for a bit later? I promised %kid1 a walk without anyone else deciding when to come home.
marriage.TwoKids_4: One picture on my desk has a dignified sun. In the other, the sun has legs and it's leaving. I like them both.$2
marriage.Good_0: I found the sweater from our first winter together. I can still pick out the stitch you fixed.
marriage.Good_1: I got enough done this morning to take a walk with you. I'll put it on the calendar before I fill the space by accident.
marriage.Good_2: Remember when you said you knew which chair I'd pick in a room full of chairs? That might be my favorite compliment.
marriage.Neutral_0: Can I leave these printouts here? If they're in your way, put them in the drawer with the scissors.
marriage.Bad_0: I've been answering people before they finish talking today. If I did that to you, I'll listen when you're ready.
engagement.0: Yes, @. I want to be the person who brings their boxes to your door and knows which key fits.$11
engagement.1: We need a song. I ruled out Sam’s battle theme, despite his formal appeal.$2
festival.spring13: I was sketching the eggs. Does that disqualify me from remembering where they are?$5
festival.spring13.spouse: If we compare notes, remember I spent ten minutes drawing a rock.
festival.spring24: I'm counting the steps under my breath. The flowers can keep a secret, right?$6
festival.spring24.spouse: Will you take my hand on the turn?
festival.summer11: I brought a spoon. Now I'm worried about how many people have the same secret-ingredient face.
festival.summer11.spouse: If supper goes wrong, let's get pizza on the way home.
festival.summer28: That lantern lights up both the waves and the dock. I wish I could draw light moving like that.
festival.summer28.spouse: Let's find a spot where we can both see. I'll put the sketchbook away.
festival.fall16: That display has six shades of orange. I may have chosen the wrong trade.
festival.fall16.spouse: Let's split something sweet after this. I spend tickets badly when I'm hungry.
festival.fall27: I'm studying how the stalls are decorated. It's definitely not an excuse to put off the maze.$6
festival.fall27.spouse: If I grab your hand, I'm just checking you're still having fun.$2
festival.winter8: I made a square snowball. Sam says that's a snowbrick.
festival.winter8.spouse: Come stand here a second. The wind is quieter by my shoulder.

villager.Abigail: Arthur made a boss that gets sad if you leave. Next time I'm bringing it a snack.

little.first: I promised we’d look for old lettering after school. Want to come with us?
